title: Determinant homomorphism from K_0 to the Picard group
statement: Let $S$ be a commutative ring. Let $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ be the abelian group of isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] $S$-modules whose localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] at every prime ideal is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of rank one, with group law induced by tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There is a group homomorphism $\det:K_0(S)\to\operatorname{Pic}(S)$, with $K_0(S)$ and its classes as constructed in [def-trf-k0-group], such that, for every finitely generated projective $S$-module $Q$ whose localizations at all prime ideals are free of rank one, $\det([Q])$ is the class of $Q$, while $\det([S])$ is the identity class represented by $S$.

The K_0 presentation is the direct-sum presentation recalled at lines 36458-36461, including the set-sized quotient-module representatives of Algebra Section 00JC (section-K-groups).

proof.text: Let $M$ be a finitely generated projective $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Choosing generators gives a surjection $S^n\to M$, which splits because $M$ is projective, so $M$ is a direct summand of a finite free module and the determinant module $\det_S(M)$ of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] is defined. That statement says $\det_S(M)$ is a finite projective module, free of rank one on the members $D(f_i)$ of a cover of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ by standard opens; for a prime $\mathfrak p\in D(f_i)$ the localization $\det_S(M)_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is the localization at $\mathfrak p$ of a free rank-one $S_{f_i}$-module, hence free of rank one over $S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Thus $\det_S(M)$ is one of the modules whose isomorphism classes form the set $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ of the statement. If $\varphi:M_1\to M_2$ is an isomorphism, the exact sequence $0\to M_1\xrightarrow{\varphi}M_2\to0\to0$ and the cited statement, which sets $\det_S(0)=S$, give $\det_S(M_1)\cong\det_S(M_1)\otimes_SS\cong\det_S(M_2)$; so the class of $\det_S(M)$ depends only on the isomorphism class of $M$. For finite projective $Q',Q''$ the split exact sequence $0\to Q'\to Q'\oplus Q''\to Q''\to0$ gives, again by the cited statement, $\det_S(Q')\otimes_S\det_S(Q'')\cong\det_S(Q'\oplus Q'')$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: Let $Q$ be finitely generated projective with $Q_{\mathfrak p}$ free of rank one for every prime $\mathfrak p$. On a member $D(f)$ of the cover used in [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence], $Q_f$ is finite free, say with basis of size $n$; if $S_f\ne0$, then for a prime $\mathfrak p\in D(f)$ the module $Q_{\mathfrak p}=(Q_f)_{\mathfrak p}$ is free of rank $n$ and of rank one over the nonzero ring $S_{\mathfrak p}$, so $n=1$; if $S_f=0$ all modules over it are zero. So the top exterior power on $D(f)$ is $\wedge^1_{S_f}(Q_f)$, and $\iota:Q_f\to\wedge^1_{S_f}(Q_f)$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. On overlaps the gluing maps are $\wedge^1$ of change-of-basis maps, i.e. under $\iota$ the identity transition maps of the localizations of $Q$; hence the glued module $\det_S(Q)$ is isomorphic to $Q$. In particular $\det_S(S)\cong S$. For $n\ge1$ the split exact sequence $0\to S^{n-1}\to S^n\to S\to0$ and the cited statement give $\det_S(S^n)\cong\det_S(S^{n-1})\otimes_S\det_S(S)\cong\det_S(S^{n-1})\otimes_SS\cong\det_S(S^{n-1})$, so by induction from $\det_S(S^0)=\det_S(0)=S$ we get $\det_S(S^n)\cong S$ for all $n\ge0$.

proof.text: The set $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ of the statement is an abelian group under $\otimes_S$ with identity the class of $S$. Closure: if $L_1,L_2$ are in it, choose complements with $L_1\oplus L_1'\cong S^a$ and $L_2\oplus L_2'\cong S^b$ (Step 1); since tensor product distributes over finite direct sums, $L_1\otimes_SL_2$ is a direct summand of $S^a\otimes_SS^b\cong S^{ab}$, hence finitely generated projective; and for every prime $\mathfrak p$, $(L_1\otimes_SL_2)_{\mathfrak p}\cong(L_1)_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}(L_2)_{\mathfrak p}\cong S_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}S_{\mathfrak p}\cong S_{\mathfrak p}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product]. The class of $L_1\otimes_SL_2$ depends only on the classes of $L_1,L_2$ by the functoriality $f\otimes\mathrm{id}$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and the canonical associativity, commutativity and unit isomorphisms $S\otimes_SL\cong L$ of the tensor product give a commutative monoid with identity $[S]$. Inverses: for $L$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ choose $L'$ with $L\oplus L'\cong S^n$ (Step 1). By Steps 1 and 2, $L\otimes_S\det_S(L')\cong\det_S(L)\otimes_S\det_S(L')\cong\det_S(L\oplus L')\cong\det_S(S^n)\cong S$, and $\det_S(L')$ lies in $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ by Step 1; so its class is an inverse of the class of $L$.

proof.text: Send the generator of [def-trf-k0-group] indexed by the isomorphism class of a finite projective $Q$ to the class of $\det_S(Q)$ in the abelian group $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ of Step 3; this is well defined on isomorphism classes by Step 1. It extends uniquely to a homomorphism from the free abelian group $\mathbf Z^{(I_S)}$ of [def-trf-abelian-group-presentation], and by the direct-sum isomorphism of Step 1 it kills every relation $e_a+e_b-e_{a\oplus b}$; hence it descends to a group homomorphism $\det:K_0(S)=G(I_S,I_S\times I_S,r)\to\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ with $\det([Q])=[\det_S(Q)]$. By Step 2, $\det([Q])$ is the class of $Q$ when every $Q_{\mathfrak p}$ is free of rank one, and $\det([S])=[S]$, the identity of $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ by Step 3.
